summary: Pass 1 triage of a packed PE32 GUI binary (390144 bytes, image base 0x400000, entry 0x401510). The sample uses an obfuscated entry point (ROR-based gate, conditional __halt/JUMPOUT), self-modifies its .idata import table, and routes control through a deep linear chain of ~49 single-call wrapper functions. A single non-trivial function, sub_401B84 at 0x401B84, implements a custom XOR+add+byteswap decode loop that transforms 1724 bytes sourced from byte_401ED1 (end of .text) into a heap-derived buffer. The .rdata section is anomalously large (407KB) and rw-mapped but contains only the import-name/API strings; no meaningful data strings, no embedded configuration, and no MZ/PE header were found. Multiple GlobalFlags(NULL) anti-debug checks and a LoadLibraryW-based dynamic API resolution path are present. Unpacking is required before execution logic can be assessed.

findings.title: Sample identity and basic file format
findings.description: The target is a PE32 GUI binary for Intel 80386, 390144 bytes, image base 0x400000, entry point 0x401510 (start). MD5 306e82406a4734021f89939fd8361269, SHA256 000d6230792fefff601c0e5e87369196fdd5cfb484fdd87916a080d8b9ffc1c6.
findings.reasoning: IDA survey_binary reports arch 32, base 0x400000, entry start at 0x401510, and matches the SHA256 against the file. prepare-env stage independently recorded PE32 GUI Intel 80386.

evidence.observation: survey_binary: arch=32, base_address=0x400000, image_size=0xc9000, entrypoint start at 0x401510, sha256 matches target.

findings.title: Anomalous section layout indicates packing
findings.description: The binary has a tiny executable .text section (0x2000 = 8KB) but a 407KB .rdata section (0x4030A8-0x46B000) mapped read/write. .idata is 0xA8 bytes. All strings found are API/module names only; no meaningful data strings exist in the binary.
findings.reasoning: A 407KB rw section in an 8KB-code binary is anomalous. Sampled bytes in .rdata beyond the import-thunk/API-name region (0x4030A8-0x403500) are zero, suggesting the region is reserved for runtime-decoded payload expansion or mapped overlay rather than static data.

evidence.observation: Segments: .text 0x401000-0x403000 rx (8192B), .idata 0x403000-0x4030A8 rw, .rdata 0x4030A8-0x46B000 rw (407640B), .data 0x46B000-0x46C000 rw. Only 43 total strings, all API/module names.

limitations: Only a sample of .rdata bytes was read; full section contents not exhaustively mapped.

findings.title: Obfuscated entry point control flow
findings.description: Entry function start (0x401510) writes 0 to the LOWORD of the NSPStartup_1 import slot in .idata, then computes a branch condition via __ROR4__ of a dword, with conditional __halt() and JUMPOUT(0x401086) paths.
findings.reasoning: The decompiler reports 'write access to const memory detected'. The obfuscated gate routes control to sub_40108C only when the rotated value compares equal to 0x50; otherwise the process halts. This is control-flow obfuscation typical of a packed/self-modifying loader.

evidence.observation: start(): LOWORD(NSPStartup_1)=0; v1=__ROR4__(*(_DWORD*)((char*)NSPStartup_1 + *(&NSPStartup_1+15) + 28), 8); if(v1<0x50) __halt(); if(v1<=0x50) JUMPOUT(0x401086); return sub_40108C().

limitations: The runtime value of the ROR operand cannot be resolved statically; actual branch outcome requires dynamic observation.

findings.title: Custom decode loop in sub_401B84
findings.description: sub_401B84 (0x401B84, 159 bytes, 4 basic blocks, cyclomatic complexity 2) is the only non-trivial function. It decodes 1724 bytes from byte_401ED1 into a heap-derived buffer using a custom chained algorithm: for each DWORD, out = (src ^ key) + 1, then key = byteswap(out). Seed key 0x22CC816A.
findings.reasoning: The assembly confirms a loop of 0x6BC (1724) bytes: mov edi,22CC456Ah; loop body xor eax,[edx]; add eax,1; mov [ebx],eax; bswap edi. The output buffer is derived from an obfuscated HeapCreate/WriteFile-import pointer computation ((char*)&HeapCreate - 2). The decoded output is likely shellcode or a first-stage PE stub.

evidence.observation: Loop: v6=1724; while(v6){ v6-=4; *v4=(*(_DWORD*)v3 ^ v5)+1; v7=*v4; v3+=4; ++v4; v5=_byteswap_ulong(v7); }. Disasm: mov edi,22CC456Ah; push 6BCh; xor eax,[edx]; add eax,1; mov [ebx],eax; bswap edi.

limitations: Decoded payload content not materialized statically; exact purpose (shellcode vs PE) requires dynamic capture.

findings.title: Anti-debug via GlobalFlags(NULL) checks
findings.description: GlobalFlags(0) is invoked from at least six locations across the wrapper chain (sub_401038, sub_401624, sub_40172C, sub_4018E0, sub_401B38, sub_401E38). GlobalFlags(NULL) returns the global heap flags; under a debugger-managed heap these flags can reflect debug allocation behavior.
findings.reasoning: Calling GlobalFlags with a NULL handle is a known anti-debug heuristic. The repeated placement across independent wrapper chains indicates the check may gate multiple code paths.

sources.location: IDA decompile of sub_401038, sub_401624, sub_40172C, sub_4018E0, sub_401B38, sub_401E38

limitations: Heuristic interpretation; GlobalFlags could also be used for heap sizing rather than purely for anti-debug.

findings.title: Import table self-modification at entry
findings.description: The entry function writes to the NSPStartup_1 slot in .idata (0x403094). Multiple import thunks are aliased to NSPStartup from PNRPNSP.dll, and the loader computes function pointers via arithmetic on import-address entries (e.g., (char*)&HeapCreate - 2 used as the WriteFile routine).
findings.reasoning: Writing to an import slot and using import-address arithmetic to derive callable pointers is a loader self-modification pattern that obscures statically visible API usage. sub_40108C calls through a vtable-derived pointer passing LoadLibraryW as an argument, indicating dynamic API resolution.

sources.location: IDA decompile start and sub_40108C / sub_401B84

findings.title: Deep single-call wrapper chain
findings.description: The executable graph is a near-linear chain of ~49 wrapper functions, each ~0x38-0x50 bytes calling the next with imported-API call sites as filler (CloseHandle(0), FindClose(0), ReleaseMutex(0), SetFocus(0), etc.). Root chain: start -> sub_40108C -> sub_4013DC -> sub_4019DC -> sub_4012B4 -> sub_401D04 -> sub_401AB4 -> sub_401E38 -> sub_401C2C -> sub_401770 -> sub_401844 -> sub_40121C -> sub_401E70 -> sub_40138C -> sub_4011DC -> sub_401428 (recursive, depth 20).
findings.reasoning: The pattern of chained wrappers each making a single next call with API calls used as decoy filler is characteristic of a flattened/obfuscated loader. sub_401428 is the deepest node and heads the subgraph containing the decode loop.

evidence.observation: 50 total functions, 49 unnamed, call graph 21 nodes/48 edges from start root, deepest node sub_401428 at depth 20.

limitations: Wrapper 'filler' API calls (with null handles) are likely decoys; their anti-debug role is uncertain.

findings.title: No embedded configuration or PE payload in static data
findings.description: No MZ/PE header, URL, IP, registry path, or meaningful configuration string was found via string search or binary search of .rdata. The 1724-byte encrypted blob at byte_401ED1 is the only in-file data beyond API names.
findings.reasoning: The payload is expected to appear only after the sub_401B84 decode runs, targeting a heap-derived buffer. Configuration (C2, paths) is expected to be embedded in or derived from the decoded payload, not present in static file data.

sources.location: IDA find_regex all strings / get_bytes .rdata sample

evidence.observation: All 43 strings are API/module names. get_bytes at 0x4030A8 shows a thunk table then zeroes; no MZ signature found in sampled .rdata.

limitations: Only sampled regions of .rdata were examined; a fully exhaustive byte scan was not performed.
